    Hosted portability follow-up — 3 November 2026

    Source: MAINTENANCE.md

    Published baseline: c97cfa2. The earlier audit below is historical; its publication-authorization statements predate that main commit.

    The Windows job reported two traversal failures because base R’s Sys.readlink() returns empty strings on Windows. Manifest discovery now uses the explicit fs dependency to refuse native file/directory links, dangling links and junctions; root and member containment use the same canonical path_real operation. Within-root aliases remain refused under the existing no-link contract. The two observed Windows fixture-cleanup warnings are addressed with fs::link_delete, without removing or weakening assertions.

    The pkgdown job failed before building because it could not resolve cellspecR. Its R setup now declares the CTTIR r-universe, matching the existing R-check workflow. The new synthetic link regressions fail five assertions against the frozen baseline. The complete local suite passed 1,116 assertions with no failures or warnings; the native Windows junction case is reserved for Windows. Shared house lint and workflow validation pass, and independent source review checked the fs/libuv Windows semantics. Coverage reached 96.65%, above the 95% gate. The complete source-package check passed with zero errors, zero warnings and one submission/dependency-availability NOTE. Exact-head hosted Windows qualification remains separate from these macOS results.

    No public scientific API, data schema, R minimum or release/deployment gate was changed. These path checks do not establish race-free OS-level containment or qualify every possible filesystem reparse-point type.

    Contracts: R readlink behavior and fs file-type queries.

    Maintenance audit — 2 November 2026

    Repository CTTIR/gatekeepR; base 9514a37b688f2dc3abecfaf0e0153a0e0835bb91. Original clean checkout is preserved. Changes are isolated on maintenance/public-readiness-20261030; publication is not authorized.

    Purpose and baseline

    The promised path is source measurements -> supported marker thresholds -> classification -> reviewer decisions -> checkpoint -> locked export -> verified replay. Append-only history and content-addressed records must preserve actual scientific meaning, not merely files with matching checksums.

    The first test attempt passed 629 assertions but encountered 17 errors, one skip and one warning while dbscan was missing; this was an incomplete environment baseline. The pinned unchanged base then passed 738 assertions with no failures or skips and one expected RNG restoration warning. Baseline logs/source and all subsequent evidence are retained in the workspace audit directory.

    Optional EBImage 4.54.0 initially failed because FFTW headers were absent. FFTW 3.3.11 was built into the audit’s private tools directory and fftwtools/EBImage installed into its private R library. No global R library or unrelated process was changed. The actual EBImage watershed and corrected embedding path ran in scientific regression checks.

    An initial suspected app export-class error was retracted: construction from a verified export succeeds. Detailed probes and raw evidence are retained under the workspace audit’s evidence/gatekeepR/.

    Strategy and acceptance, before implementation

    1. Repair scientific support, missingness, method dispatch, localization and source/score-space contracts. Use independently calculated small fixtures, multiple images and deliberately mismatched objects. Preserve source data.
    2. Repair ordered reviewer replay, undo and persistence. Verify effective calls, prior dispositions, checkpoint round trips and concurrent session ownership.
    3. Bind and verify snapshot identity, scientific content, all ledgers and review status. Rehashed tampering must fail. Preserve legacy files and document any stricter verification/re-review migration instead of silently rewriting them.
    4. Complete a bounded review UI using the same R APIs: reviewer/reason, cuts, states, structures, dispositions, undo, checkpoint, lock and current-snapshot downloads. Changes invalidate stale downloads; no automatic scientific approval or duplicate classifier. Verify the full path in a real browser.
    5. Validate package installation, manuals, vignettes, first use, optional methods, shared house lint and the existing 95% coverage gate. Independently review results and record exact commands, failures, final artifacts and limits.

    Scientific contracts precede final review/export qualification. App work may proceed against stable public APIs. Segmentation, cohort statistics, new assay panels and biological validation remain outside this maintenance release.

    Completed work and verification

    The five milestones above are complete for local readiness. Scientific support, source/score contracts, effective reviewer replay, checkpoint concurrency, content-bound exports, app controls and executable documentation were repaired. Version 1.1.0 is an unpublished development candidate. CRAN’s current source index had no gatekeepR entry on 2 November 2026; GitHub reported no releases or tags. Unverified publication metadata were corrected, and CFF 1.2.0 validation passes. The public maintainer email and ORCID are preserved.

    The final archive is .checks/readiness-5/gatekeepR_1.1.0.tar.gz (1,914,179 bytes), SHA-256 3c839b14b4097810016afe2abc5964c5dc2c4bb3503c7ebbbbdea0b35940dc7c. The final check used R 4.6.1 on aarch64 macOS 27.0.1, with audit-local dependencies. The fresh package library reused those audited dependencies; it was not an independent download of every dependency. Hosted Linux/Windows checks and older supported R versions have not been run for these commits.

    The original baseline passed its tests despite the confirmed defects. Subsequent independent review caught fractional ledger truncation, empty structure handling, render-only plot failures and ambiguous composite identities. Intermediate build failures were fixed. A documentation probe image accidentally entered one candidate archive; it was preserved outside the source tree, and the final archive was rebuilt, inspected and checked cleanly. No check was weakened.

    Benchmark totals for prepare through verified export were 2.74/2.75/9.84 seconds for 300/1,000/8,000 cells versus baseline 0.81/1.09/5.08 seconds. The main added cost is verification before publication and the additional replay payload. Sampled RSS peaked at 278 MiB. These are local observations under concurrent machine load, not a throughput guarantee. No speculative optimization was made.

    Local evidence is under the workspace audit’s evidence/gatekeepR/, including verification.json, build-check-5.log, coverage-gate.json, final-archive-inspection.json, final-first-use-5/result.json, site-manual-verification.md, performance.json and per-area independent reviews. run.sh defines the private R library and tools used; build-check-5.R, coverage-gate.R and installed-first-use.R record exact reproducible commands. The README gives the installation and first-use path. Standard checks from a prepared development environment are:

    R CMD build .
R CMD check --as-cran gatekeepR_1.1.0.tar.gz
NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'x <- covr::package_coverage(type="tests"); stopifnot(covr::percent_coverage(x) >= 95)'

    Migration and interpretation

    Version 2 exports/checkpoints and hash bindings intentionally reject legacy analytical objects. Keep original data, files and provenance. Rebuild from the original source/configuration, review changed results and write to new paths. Legacy export inspection remains available only with explicit verify = FALSE. Frozen residual models can import validated original parameter fields and file SHA without refitting; retain bindings/provenance and requalify outputs. The migration regression preserves parameter values, numerical outputs and source bytes. Exact finite score transport uses strict typed parsing; missing numeric values have a canonical representation in content hashes.

    Keep the full review ID independently to detect replacement of an entire export. Hashes do not authenticate a human reviewer. REVIEWED records a human assertion, not scientific or clinical validation. Owner locks persist after R exits; explicit takeover is appropriate only after confirming the prior process stopped.

    The development-only Remotes field was replaced with Additional_repositories for the optional cellspecR adapter, following the CRAN policies. The declared repository supplies cellspecR 1.1.0. No hosted CI, deployment, submission or publication has been performed.

    Deferred work and external readiness

    The current release excludes segmentation, new assay panels, image overlays, freehand annotation and cohort statistics. Biological assay qualification and study-specific human review remain the user’s scientific work. After all local gates pass, the next release step is review and authorization of the prepared commits, hosted platform checks on those exact commits, then submission or publication through the intended channel.
